title: Fugaro apply
description: The JSON answer of `fugaro apply` and `fugaro apply --status` (docs/composite-commands, D1560, D1568, D1569, D1575): the steps a machine still owes for the management changes made on it, and — for a run — the steps it answered. It is the document the console reads through the fence (D1569, one read, `fugaro apply --status --json`), so it is a contract and not a debug dump: every member is written on every arm, a member is added and never repointed, and the version says which shape the reader is holding (CLAUDE.md, F9). Every object here is closed for the reason the pending-steps document's are: the console and this binary are the only readers, the format decodes strictly, and a member neither knows is an error rather than a figure drawn from a guess. It carries no value and no secret: an entry names the change that asked for a step and never what was set (D1570).

version.description: The document's own version, so a reader that was built against one shape refuses another rather than drawing a wrong figure with no error (CLAUDE.md: a field never changes meaning).

project.description: The Fugaro project name this answer is about (config.ProjectNameRE). It is one half of the pair every entry of the record is bound to, and a record whose entries name another pair is refused rather than run (D1575).

gcp_project.description: The GCP project ID of the installation this answer is about, and the other half of that pair.

recorded.description: Whether a record of what this machine owes is on disk at all. A machine that never made a management change and one whose record was deleted read the same — nothing is owed — and this is what tells the two apart in the answer; a reader must not read `false` as "everything is live" (D1575).

current.description: Whether the record was stamped against the project config as it stands. False means the config changed since the last `fugaro apply` that finished, so what the record owes may be older than the config — or newer than it, when a change was just saved. The stamp is the hash of the local project config's bytes, and `fugaro doctor` is the command that compares it (D1575).

pending.description: What is still owed, in the order the steps run (internal/apply's Order over internal/initflow's own stage order), and it is written even when it is empty: `[]` is "nothing is owed", which is a different answer from a record that could not be read. Two changes that owe the same step leave one entry, so the steps dedupe (spec rule 3).

step.description: The step's name: one of internal/initflow's stage names, or `catalog-build`, the one step that is not a stage — the billable Cloud Build of a catalog image, which `fugaro update` never runs (D1577). It is deliberately not an enum, for the reason the pending-steps document's is not: the vocabulary is initflow's, and a copy of it here would be the second registry of stages D1561 rules out.
step.$comment: apply.CatalogBuild in internal/apply/steps.go, and initflow.Names in internal/initflow/stage.go.

kind.description: What `key` names: a key of the settings registry (internal/settings), or a resource type a management command manages.

key.description: The setting key as `fugaro settings` spells it, or a resource type. It is the change's subject and never its value (D1570). The human arm of this command prints it through safetext, because it is a person's own text landing on a terminal (D1575).

applied.description: The steps a run answered, in the order they ran. It is absent for `--status`, which runs none, and it is never present-and-empty for a run: a run that answered nothing has nothing to report as applied. A step is here only when its own answer said the work is done — `changed`, `done` or `skipped`, the last being the read-only check finding nothing to do (D1575) — and a step that failed, was blocked or was left for the person is in `pending` instead (D1563).
